title: Parametron phase bits held by a shared resonant pump
idea: Invert 'a bit is a static stored quantity' -> the bit is the phase (0 or pi) of a sustained sub-harmonic oscillation. On-die high-Q LC or AlN bulk-acoustic parametrons are pumped at 2f by one shared resonant clock tree; each locks into one of two phases, written by a tiny seed injection and read by mixing against a reference phase.
why: Removes the capacitor charge wall and refresh entirely (facts 1, 3): the pump regenerates every bit every cycle and the resonant tree recycles most pump energy; standby cost scales with 1/Q rather than leakage tails.

title: Vertical CCD strings on 3D-NAND tooling as capacitorless 3D DRAM
idea: Invert 'every bit needs its own capacitor and access transistor at a fixed site' -> bits are charge packets that march. A vertical oxide-semiconductor or epitaxial channel threads 64-128 word-plane tiers clocked as a 3-phase CCD, so each pillar holds dozens of packets shifted to one sense/regenerate node at its top.
why: A 3D DRAM with no capacitor and no lateral transistor (fact 2) built in depreciated 3D-NAND fabs; area per bit ~pillar pitch^2/tiers gives >5x DDR5 density, refresh happens automatically every lap; latency ~tiers x shift time (~30-60 ns).

title: Antiferroelectric capacitor parked at its field-induced transition knee
idea: Invert 'the capacitor dielectric operates linearly around zero bias' -> park it on a phase transition. A ZrO2-rich antiferroelectric capacitor is DC-biased by the plate line to the edge of its AFE-to-FE transition, where dP/dE (effective k) is 5-10x the linear value, and data is stored as a small +/- swing around that knee.
why: Recovers the k~70 regime fact 1 demands, so ~5 fF fits at AR ~20-30 instead of 60-75 using existing HfZrO ALD; risks are hysteresis loss, temperature drift of the knee and fatigue.

title: Contactless tunneling nano-relay isolates the storage capacitor in vacuum
idea: Invert 'the access device is a leaky semiconductor junction' -> isolate the storage node with a vacuum gap. A vertical electrostatic nano-relay in the BEOL never touches: it closes from ~5 nm to ~1 nm so charge tunnels in/out, and when open the vacuum gap has no junction, GIDL or trap-assisted leakage.
why: Kills the <=13 fA leakage tail that forces refresh (fact 3): retention becomes dielectric-limited (hours), recovering 10-20% bandwidth and refresh energy; no contact means no wear, keeping endurance effectively unlimited.

title: Leakage decay as built-in recency weighting for analog KV caches
idea: Invert 'charge decay is a failure that refresh must undo' -> make decay part of the math. KV-cache and state-space values are stored as un-refreshed analog charge whose leakage time constant is programmed per bank by body bias, so stored magnitude decays exponentially with token age, implementing the recency weighting (decay gates, ALiBi-like bias) models already learn.
why: Eliminates refresh for the largest AI memory consumer (fact 3) and stores 4-6 analog bits per cell, multiplying effective capacity 4-6x for inference KV caches.

title: Capacitorless 50-microsecond cells sized to transient tensor lifetimes
idea: Invert 'every bit must survive 64 ms' -> design a cell that only lasts ~50 us. A 2-transistor node using only the read-transistor gate capacitance (~0.1 fF, no capacitor) holds activations, gradients and attention scratch whose lifetime is microseconds; the compiler guarantees consumption or rewrite before expiry and hardware timestamps flag expired lines.
why: Removes the capacitor (fact 1) and all refresh for transient data, which is a majority of accelerator traffic; ~2-3x density over 1T1C on a logic-compatible process.

title: Solid-state Williams tube: charge puddles in an unpatterned film
idea: Invert 'each bit needs a discrete patterned capacitor' -> store charge puddles in a continuous film. A semi-insulating high-k layer (rho ~1e15 ohm-cm) lies between orthogonal row/column electrode grids with a thin rectifying MIM-diode interlayer; charge injected at a crossing stays local because lateral RC spreading takes longer than seconds, like the 1947 Williams CRT memory in solid form.
why: Deletes the HAR capacitor etch and per-cell isolation (facts 1, 4): a 4F^2 crosspoint without access transistors and several fewer critical masks.

title: Frequency-addressed nano-resonator cells read in parallel by FFT
idea: Invert 'addressing is spatial, one access transistor per cell' -> address by frequency. Each cell on a shared line is a nano-resonator with a unique designed frequency; the bit is charge parked on its electrostatic spring (shifting frequency ~1%), and a single broadband chirp plus FFT reads all 64 cells of a line non-destructively at once.
why: Removes access transistors and most row decoding (periphery ~49%, fact 7), and replaces destructive reads (fact 8) with parallel non-destructive ones; resonator footprint is the main risk.

title: Resonant-tunneling-diode pinning lets all cells self-restore simultaneously
idea: Invert 'refresh means reading each row and writing it back' -> let every cell restore itself at once. Each storage node connects to a shared pulsed rail through a series pair of BEOL resonant-tunneling diodes whose N-shaped I-V gives two stable node voltages; a ~1 ns global rail pulse every few ms snaps all cells to the nearer level without sensing or row activation.
why: Eliminates refresh activations, freeing 10-20% bandwidth and most of the ~46 fJ/bit refresh energy (fact 3), and makes refresh-based row-hammer mitigation nearly free (fact 9); risk is RTD peak-to-valley uniformity at room temperature.

title: Protonic shuttle cell stores protons, not electrons
idea: Invert 'the stored carrier is an electron' -> store protons. A 5 nm phosphorus-doped SiO2 solid acid lets protons shuttle under ~1 V/nm pulses into or out of an Nb2O5 or WO3 nano-channel in nanoseconds, setting a non-volatile conductance; protons intercalate without breaking host bonds, the hoped route to near-unlimited endurance.
why: Refresh-free, non-destructive read, ~fJ writes (facts 3, 8, 10); Nb2O5 option avoids the tungsten chokepoint; risk is proving >1e15-cycle endurance.

title: Solid-electrolyte double-layer capacitor replaces dielectric polarization
idea: Invert 'capacitance comes from electronic dielectric polarization' -> use an ionic double layer. A 3-5 nm solid proton or Li-ion electrolyte between electrodes forms an electric double layer of ~10-20 uF/cm^2, versus ~2.6 uF/cm^2 effective in today's pillar stacks, so 5 fF needs only an AR ~10-15 cup.
why: Attacks the capacitor charge wall (fact 1) by 4-8x per area, removing the hardest HAR etch steps; risk is whether nanometer EDLs charge in nanoseconds and survive unlimited cycling.

title: Liquid-nitrogen 77 K DRAM pods with planar capacitors
idea: Invert 'memory runs at room temperature' -> run DRAM at 77 K in liquid-nitrogen pods (nitrogen is abundant, unlike helium). Junction, GIDL and subthreshold leakage fall by >1e6, so a planar 0.3 fF capacitor retains for seconds, and steeper subthreshold slope allows ~0.6 V array and wordline swings.
why: Removes the capacitor charge wall (fact 1) and refresh (fact 3) and cuts CV^2 ~3x (fact 10); the ~10x cooling overhead at 77 K must be repaid by density and system energy gains.

title: Shallow 1 fF pillars rescued by soft-decision sensing and LDPC
idea: Invert 'every cell must read correctly on its own' -> let cells be weak and the code be smart. Etch only 1 fF, AR ~15 pillars; sense amps emit 2-bit soft information (strong/weak 0/1) to an on-die LDPC decoder over 512-bit codewords, tolerating raw BER ~1e-3 that would kill a hard-decision chip.
why: Cuts capacitor AR 4-5x (fact 1) and lets refresh stretch since weak cells become erasures (fact 3), for ~12% parity plus decoder area; decoder latency is the risk.

title: Hundred-electron bits read by room-temperature single-electron transistors
idea: Invert 'a bit needs ~30,000 stored electrons' -> store ~100. Each node is a ~20 aF floating island sensed by a single-electron transistor built from a ~1.5 nm metal cluster or molecule, whose Coulomb oscillations turn +/-100 electrons into a large current swing.
why: Eliminates the capacitor (fact 1) and cuts write energy to ~1.6e-17 J (~1000x, fact 10) at ~4F^2; room-temperature SET uniformity is the speculative part.

title: Contact-free buckled nanotube bit clamped inside a BEOL via
idea: Invert 'storage is electronic' -> store the bit as which way a beam bows. A nanotube or nanowire clamped top and bottom in a BEOL via under compressive pre-strain buckles left or right; side electrodes flip it electrostatically and read the asymmetric capacitance, with no contact ever made, so no stiction or wear.
why: Non-volatile with zero leakage (fact 3), elastic bending can survive >1e15 cycles in principle, and it stacks in BEOL with no silicon transistor per bit (fact 2); thermal stability below 20 nm is the risk.

title: Ferroelastic twin-variant bits read through strain-gated 2D channels
idea: Invert 'a bit is held as electrical or magnetic order' -> hold it as a crystal's shape. A ferroelastic film has two twin variants with orthogonal spontaneous strain; a piezoelectric AlN micro-actuator under each cell toggles the variant, and the strain state is read by the mobility shift of a 2D-semiconductor channel laminated on top.
why: No charge to leak (fact 3), non-destructive read (fact 8), diffusionless twin switching hints at very high endurance; nano-scale actuation and twin-wall pinning are speculative.

title: Buried germanium quantum well confines holes without any p-n junction
idea: Invert 'retention is set by junction leakage' -> set it by a band offset. Holes are stored in a compressively strained Ge quantum well 5 nm below a Si channel; the ~0.5 eV valence-band offset confines them with no p-n junction, so the defect-driven GIDL/junction tail becomes designed thermionic escape with retention ~exp(dEv/kT).
why: Capacitorless 4F^2 vertical cell (fact 1) whose retention is set by epitaxy rather than random defects, tightening the leakage tail and cutting refresh (fact 3).

title: Altermagnet bits read by spin-split tunneling with zero net moment
idea: Invert 'magnetic memory needs net magnetization to be read' -> store the bit in an altermagnet whose moments cancel. MnTe or RuO2-class altermagnets have zero net moment yet spin-split bands, so a tunnel junction reads Neel orientation by TMR and spin-splitter torque writes it; no stray field permits ~10 nm pitch and wear-free, THz-fast switching.
why: Non-volatile, unlimited endurance, dense without dipolar crosstalk and immune to row-hammer-style disturbance (fact 9); MnTe avoids ruthenium scarcity; room-temperature TMR magnitude is the risk.

title: Sealed charge-conserving double-island cell with no path to ground
idea: Invert 'the storage node connects to the outside through a leaky path' -> make the bit a sealed, charge-conserving pair. Two metal nano-islands share one tunnel barrier and have no other conductive path; the bit is which island holds the excess electrons (dipole up/down), flipped by a field pulse from adjacent gates and read by capacitive coupling to a sense FET.
why: Charge cannot leak off a sealed pair, so refresh disappears and endurance is unlimited (facts 1, 3) at ~10 nm cells; room-temperature retention needs sub-5 nm islands and engineered barriers.

title: Persistent-current flux bits cooled by cryocoolers, not helium
idea: Invert 'bits must live in charge or polarization of matter' -> store them as a quantized persistent current. NbN or MgB2 nanowire loops hold one flux quantum clockwise or counter-clockwise with zero dissipation, written by kinetic-inductance switching and read by a nanowire cryotron, cooled by closed-cycle cryocoolers instead of liquid helium.
why: Zero static power, unlimited endurance and ~10 aJ switching (fact 10), fitting cryogenic AI accelerators; avoids the Qatar helium chokepoint; density and ~400 W/W 4 K overhead (MgB2 at 20 K cuts it ~10x) are the risks.

title: Rank-order charge encoding survives common-mode leakage drift
idea: Invert 'each cell's charge level carries data absolutely' -> encode data in the relative order of charges in a group. Four cells written to four distinct analog levels encode one of 24 permutations (4.58 bits per 4 cells); because leakage drags all levels down together, the rank order survives long after fixed thresholds fail, and a read is a local comparator sort.
why: Stretches refresh interval ~4-10x (fact 3) and adds ~15% bits per cell (cost/bit); tail cells that break order are handled by a light outer code.

title: Self-assembled random nanodot capacitors with post-fab address remapping
idea: Invert 'every cell must be lithographically placed, identical and good' -> accept random cells and map them. Block-copolymer self-assembly drops ~15 nm metal nanodot capacitors at random over a relaxed 40 nm crossbar; built-in self-test classifies each crossing (empty, one dot, several, retention class) and writes a remap table so the controller uses only good sites.
why: Removes critical-dimension lithography for the storage layer (EUV, fact 4) and turns variability into a mapped resource instead of yield loss; map overhead and drift are the risks.

title: Logic-die decoupling capacitors double as on-demand scratch memory
idea: Invert 'storage elements must be dedicated memory cells' -> reuse the capacitors already on every logic die. An accelerator's deep-trench/MIM decap is split into ~50 fF segments with access switches, so idle decap banks act as eDRAM-like scratch when the supply-noise budget allows and revert to decoupling during load surges.
why: ~15% of an 800 mm^2 die at ~500 nF/mm^2 is ~1e9 storable bits (~100+ MB) of near-compute memory with ~zero added wafer area, cutting data-movement energy (fact 5) and DRAM demand.

title: Anodized aluminum nanopore capacitors replace plasma-etched silicon pillars
idea: Invert 'HAR capacitors must be plasma-etched into a silicon wafer' -> let electrochemistry grow them on aluminum. Anodizing an aluminum plate self-organizes hexagonal pores (~40-60 nm pitch, AR 100+) in minutes; ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN lines each pore as a cup capacitor, the aluminum is the common plate and heat spreader, and oxide-TFT access and wiring are built on the planarized top.
why: Delivers AR >100, past fact 1's AR-115 regime, with no HAR plasma etch, no EUV and no quartz-crucible silicon, cutting capacitor-module capex >10x; pore-to-TFT registration is handled by pre-patterned anodization seeds or several pores per cell.

title: Ferroelectric nematic liquid-crystal capacitors filled like LCD panels
idea: Invert 'the capacitor dielectric must be a deposited solid' -> use a liquid. Ferroelectric nematic LCs (RM734/DIO class) show apparent permittivity of 1e3-1e4; display fabs capillary-fill them into nano-trench capacitors on glass with oxide-TFT access and seal them exactly as LCD lines do.
why: If even k_eff ~300 survives at nanosecond fields, 5 fF fits in a planar or AR<5 cell (fact 1) using idle Gen-8.5/10.5 display fabs (capital); risks are dielectric relaxation speed, interfacial artifacts behind the giant k, and ionic impurities.

title: GaN-on-sapphire wide-bandgap charge cell that never needs refresh
idea: Invert 'DRAM charge is volatile and must be refreshed' -> pick a semiconductor whose 3.4 eV bandgap makes thermal generation ~1e-20 of silicon's. An AlGaN/GaN access transistor with a junctionless p-GaN storage node on cheap LED-grade sapphire holds charge for days to years while storage stays pure charge with no material wear.
why: Removes refresh power and bandwidth tax (fact 3) and makes the memory effectively non-volatile with unlimited endurance; reuses U.S./allied LED and RF GaN lines instead of silicon DRAM fabs; dense enhancement-mode GaN and interface traps are the risks.

title: Lithium-niobate domain-wall conduction gives non-destructive ferroelectric reads
idea: Invert 'ferroelectric bits must be read destructively by switching' -> read the walls, not the domains. In thin-film lithium niobate on insulator, a written nanodomain creates charged conductive domain walls between two lateral electrodes; the bit is presence or absence of wall current (on/off >1e4), read without switching polarization.
why: Non-destructive read removes the write-back half of every access (fact 8) and read fatigue; non-volatile so no refresh (fact 3); LNOI wafers come from the photonics supply chain, not silicon; write endurance and sub-30 nm wall stability are the risks.

title: Polar-vortex handedness bits in oxide superlattices on scandate substrates
idea: Invert 'a ferroelectric bit is polarization up or down' -> store the chirality of a polar vortex. PbTiO3/SrTiO3 superlattices grown on DyScO3 or SrTiO3 substrates form ~10 nm vortex tubes whose left/right handedness is a topologically protected binary state, switched by a curled field from twin gate electrodes and read by a chirality-dependent capacitance/piezo asymmetry.
why: Topological protection gives retention and disturb immunity at ~10 nm pitch (density, fact 9) with no capacitor; electrical chirality read/write at speed is unproven.

title: Sliding-ferroelectric bilayer hBN grown roll-to-roll on copper foil
idea: Invert 'polarization switching moves ions inside a unit cell and fatigues' -> slide whole atomic layers by one bond length. Parallel-stacked bilayer hBN or 3R-MoS2 grown by roll-to-roll CVD on copper foil and laminated onto glass or polyimide flips out-of-plane polarization as layers glide between AB and BA registry, a bond-preserving motion reported to resist fatigue; a 2D channel below reads it non-destructively.
why: Atom-thin, non-volatile, potentially fatigue-free sub-1 V storage (facts 3, 8, 10) on a non-silicon substrate; domain pinning and large-area stacking control are the risks.

title: Voltage-written magnetoelectric chromia bits grown epitaxially on sapphire
idea: Invert 'magnetic bits need current to write' -> write with voltage alone. Cr2O3 grows epitaxially on corundum sapphire; its antiferromagnetic order is reversed by an electric field in a small magnetic bias (magnetoelectric switching), and its boundary magnetization is read by anomalous Hall voltage in a 2 nm Pt overlayer.
why: Non-volatile, effectively unlimited endurance (no ion motion or barrier wear), write energy ~fJ capacitive instead of MRAM's ~100 fJ-pJ (fact 10), no silicon or tungsten; the ~307 K Neel point needs boron doping and the read signal is small.

title: Gen-10.5 display glass memory trades density for cheap area
idea: Invert 'cost per bit comes from shrinking the cell' -> buy area instead. A Gen-10.5 glass sheet is ~9.6 m^2 (~140 300-mm wafers); build 1T1C cells at ~1 um^2 with planar 20 fF MIM capacitors and IGZO access (retention minutes, refresh nearly gone), giving ~1 TB of cells per sheet in under-utilized display fabs.
why: At ~$100/m^2 backplane cost that is under ~$1/GB of raw cells with no EUV or HAR etch (facts 1, 4) and no new $15B fab; micron lines limit speed and energy, so it serves as a CXL capacity tier.

title: Self-rolling nanomembrane Swiss-roll capacitors on polymer foil
idea: Invert 'a 3D capacitor must be etched deep into a substrate' -> deposit it flat and let strain roll it up. A strained bilayer (SiNx stress layer plus TiN/HfZrO/TiN stack) patterned on a sacrificial polymer releases and curls into a 5-10 turn micro-tube, multiplying electrode area 10-20x per footprint; whole arrays roll in parallel on polyimide or glass.
why: Reaches fact-1 capacitance from planar deposition plus one release step (EUV-free, low capex) on any substrate; roll diameters below ~200 nm are hard, so it suits a cheap capacity tier.

title: Insulating garnet racetracks shift magnetic domains without Joule heating
idea: Invert 'magnetic memory needs metallic magnets on silicon' -> use an insulating ferrimagnet. Thulium-iron-garnet nanowires, sputter-crystallized on glass or grown on garnet, carry dozens of domains each, driven at >1 km/s by spin-orbit torque from a Pt underlayer, so one read/write junction per track replaces one access transistor per bit.
why: 32-64 bits per access device shrinks periphery and raises density (fact 7); non-volatile, unlimited endurance and 10-100x lower damping than metal magnets; domain-position errors and gadolinium in GGG substrates (favor glass) are the risks.

title: Spin-crossover molecular films switching high and low spin states
idea: Invert 'the bit is a charge, polarization or magnetic direction' -> store it as a molecule's spin state. Room-temperature-hysteretic Fe(II) spin-crossover complexes vacuum-sublimed onto glass or polymer flip between low and high spin (with ~10% volume and large conductance change) under a gate-induced charge or strain pulse inside their hysteresis loop, read by tunneling current.
why: Non-volatile inside the hysteresis window, ~2 nm molecular cells, no scarce elements and low-temperature processing on any substrate; field-driven switching speed and room-temperature margins are speculative.

title: Vacuum-channel field-emission access to vacuum-isolated storage electrodes
idea: Invert 'the storage node must sit in solid insulator next to a semiconductor' -> put it in vacuum. Each cell is a sealed nano-cavity on glass where a sharp emitter faces the floating storage electrode across a ~20 nm vacuum channel, gated so field emission charges or discharges the node; when off, vacuum conducts nothing.
why: Removes junction leakage and its refresh (fact 3), radiation- and temperature-immune, no silicon wafer; emitter uniformity, nano-cavity sealing and ~10 V emission fields are the risks.

title: Redox-molecule monolayers store quantized electrons on ITO glass
idea: Invert 'a capacitor holds a continuous amount of charge' -> store discrete electrons in molecules. A self-assembled monolayer of multi-state redox molecules (porphyrin or ferrocene triads) on ITO-coated glass holds 2-4 discrete oxidation states per site, giving up to 2 bits per cell at ~1e14 e/cm^2, read by redox current peaks at characteristic voltages.
why: ~10-20x the charge per area of a planar dielectric (fact 1), so no HAR capacitor, plus chemistry-defined multilevel cells; solid-state contacts, nanosecond kinetics and 1e15-cycle molecular stability are the risks.

title: Triple-barrier resonant-tunneling III-V charge node on GaAs substrates
idea: Invert 'a retention barrier must be thick so writes need high voltage' -> make it thick but resonantly transparent at one voltage. An InAs/AlSb triple-barrier stack on GaAs or InP lets electrons enter an InAs storage well only when ~2.5 V aligns quantized levels, while the ~2.1 eV AlSb offset holds charge for years at zero bias.
why: Non-volatile charge with ~100x lower write energy than flash and high endurance (no oxide trap generation), usable as refresh-free DRAM (facts 3, 10) on U.S. III-V RF/optoelectronic lines; builds on ULTRARAM-type prior art.

title: Moire superlattice traps self-assemble a ten-nanometer bit lattice
idea: Invert 'cells must be lithographically patterned' -> let a twist angle draw them. A twisted hBN/WSe2 stack on glass forms a moire potential with ~10 nm period, each minimum a trap holding a few electrons; relaxed-pitch crossbar gates address blocks and an adjacent 2D charge sensor reads occupancy.
why: Lithography-free ~1e12 sites/cm^2 (density, EUV elimination, fact 4); room-temperature retention needs >100 meV moire depth and single-site addressing is unsolved.

title: Two-terminal threshold-switch gated capacitors in crosspoint arrays on glass
idea: Invert 'every capacitor needs a three-terminal access transistor' -> gate it with a two-terminal ovonic threshold switch. A GeSe-class OTS in series with each MIM capacitor stays off below ~1.5 V and snaps on in <1 ns above it, forming a stackable 4F^2 1S1C crosspoint built at low temperature on glass, foil or ceramic.
why: Removes the access transistor (facts 2, 4) so tiers stack like 3D crosspoint without crystalline silicon; OTS off-current must reach ~fA or retention collapses to milliseconds, and threshold drift limits endurance.

title: Water-released single-crystal BST membranes stacked as capacitor tiers
idea: Invert 'high-k must be deposited polycrystalline in place' -> grow perfect crystal elsewhere and transfer it. Epitaxial (Ba,Sr)TiO3 on a water-soluble Sr3Al2O6 sacrificial layer is released as a freestanding membrane (k ~300-1000 vs ~40 for ALD ZrO2), laminated onto glass or foil carriers under oxide-TFT access, and the growth substrate is reused.
why: Beats fact 1's k~70 target with margin so capacitors go planar or AR<10; consumes no silicon wafer and reuses the growth wafer >50x (capital, quartz-crucible chokepoint); thin-film dead layers and transfer yield are the risks.

title: Charge-density-wave phase bits in 1T-TaS2 films on sapphire
idea: Invert 'storage needs atoms or spins to move' -> store the bit in collective electron order. 1T-TaS2 switches between insulating and metallic charge-density-wave states with ps-ns electrical pulses and holds each with hysteresis; wafer-scale CVD TaS2 on sapphire gives cells read by a ~10-100x resistance contrast.
why: Purely electronic reconfiguration promises unlimited endurance, sub-ns writes and tiny volumes; room-temperature bistability (strain/doping-engineered hysteresis near the 350 K transition) is speculative.

title: Complementary oxide-TFT static latch cells on cheap glass panels
idea: Invert 'working memory must be 1T1C DRAM' -> go static where area is cheap. Pair n-type IGZO with p-type SnO or Cu2O TFTs into a 4T loadless or 6T latch on glass whose feedback holds data with zero refresh, while oxide-level leakage keeps standby to ~pW per Mb.
why: No capacitor, no refresh and no destructive read (facts 1, 3, 8) with display tooling; density ~10x below DRAM but panel area makes it a cheap capacity or AI-scratch tier; p-type oxide mobility limits cycle time to ~100 ns.

title: CuInP2S6 quadruple-well ferroelectric stores two bits per cell on mica
idea: Invert 'a ferroelectric gives two states' -> use one with four. Layered CuInP2S6 has a quadruple-well potential (low and high polarization of each sign set by Cu displacement), grown by van der Waals epitaxy on cleavable mica and read through the threshold shift of a 2D-semiconductor channel.
why: 2 bits per cell with non-destructive FET read and trap-free vdW interfaces, on a non-silicon flexible substrate; Cu migration endurance and the ~315 K Curie point are the risks.

title: Nanoimprinted sol-gel high-k cup capacitors on roll-to-roll polymer web
idea: Invert 'capacitor geometry is defined by lithography plus etch' -> stamp it. A reusable master with 30 nm x 600 nm pillars imprints cup cavities into spin-on TiO2/BaTiO3 sol-gel on polyimide web, then ALD electrodes coat them, replacing EUV and HAR plasma etch with mechanical replication at metres per minute.
why: Cuts masks, EUV and capacitor-module capex >10x (fact 4) with roll-to-roll throughput for cost/bit; AR-20 demolding defects and overlay to the TFT layer are the risks.

title: Thin-film magnetic core memory with zero transistors in the array
idea: Invert 'modern memory must be built from semiconductor transistors' -> revive coincident-current magnetic cores in thin film. Sub-micron permalloy rings electroplated around crossing X/Y/sense lines on glass or ceramic switch only when two half-currents coincide, storing the bit as flux direction with nanosecond thin-film switching and no transistor per cell.
why: Unlimited endurance, non-volatile, radiation-hard, uses only Ni, Fe and Cu (no tungsten, EUV or silicon wafer); ~1 um^2 cells make it a niche or capacity tier, and destructive read plus half-select margins are the risks.

title: Bacteria-grown magnetite nanocrystals as self-made single-domain bits
idea: Invert 'storage elements are fabricated in a fab' -> grow them. Magnetotactic bacteria biomineralize near-perfect 40-50 nm single-domain magnetite crystals at room temperature from iron salts; purified magnetosomes are placed by DNA-origami or field-guided assembly onto glass carrying spin-orbit-torque write lines and Hall read contacts.
why: Ultra-uniform nanomagnets with zero vacuum or litho capex for the storage element, abundant iron (scarce-resource intensity), non-volatile with unlimited endurance; placement precision and switching current are speculative.
